title: IBRANCE Dosing Decisions: Hold/Reduce vs Continue
instruction: For each clinical finding, decide whether the current FDA prescribing information directs the clinician to withhold or reduce the IBRANCE dose, or to continue at the current dose unchanged.

items.prompt: Grade 3 (or recurrent Grade 3) neutropenia detected on Day 1 of a treatment cycle
items.rationale: The label directs withholding IBRANCE until recovery to Grade ≤2, then resuming at the next lower dose; dose interruption/reduction is recommended for Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia.

items.prompt: Day 15 CBC in Cycle 1 shows Grade 2 (moderate) neutropenia, patient otherwise well
items.rationale: Per label, dose interruption, reduction, or delay is recommended only for patients who develop Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia, not Grade 1 or 2.

items.prompt: No more than Grade 1 or 2 neutropenia across the first 6 cycles, now due for next-cycle CBC
items.rationale: For patients with a maximum of Grade 1 or 2 neutropenia in the first 6 cycles, the label states no dose adjustment is required, and CBC monitoring shifts to every 3 months.

items.prompt: New or worsening dyspnea and cough on treatment, suspected interstitial lung disease
items.rationale: The label instructs interrupting IBRANCE immediately and evaluating the patient when new or worsening respiratory symptoms suggest pneumonitis, with permanent discontinuation for severe ILD/pneumonitis.

items.prompt: Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C) present before starting IBRANCE
items.rationale: The label specifies a reduced starting dose of 75 mg once daily (same 21 days on/7 days off schedule) for patients with Child-Pugh class C hepatic impairment.

items.prompt: Mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class A) present before starting IBRANCE
items.rationale: The label requires no dose adjustment for mild or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or B); only severe impairment (Child-Pugh C) requires a lower starting dose.

citations.title: Label: IBRANCE- palbociclib tablet, film coated - DailyMed

items.prompt: Patient requires a strong CYP3A inhibitor (e.g., itraconazole) that cannot be switched or avoided
items.rationale: Because coadministration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor substantially increases palbociclib exposure, the label directs reducing the IBRANCE dose if such a drug cannot be avoided.
